title: Delroy
desc: Half the country you had not accounted for
setting: A new man on the afternoon shift takes a phone call in a language that sounds like English and is not.

steps.speaker: Delroy
steps.es: Sorry, that was my mother. She no speak Spanish.
steps.en: Sorry, that was my mother. She does not speak Spanish.

options.es: ¿De dónde sos vos? Nunca había oído eso.
options.en: Where are you from? I had never heard that.
options.feedback: Curious, direct, and vos. It treats him as a workmate rather than a curiosity.
Close, and a bit off. It sounds like English and it is not, and he gets asked that daily.
He is Nicaraguan. That guess is the one he has been correcting since he arrived in Managua.

steps.speaker: Delroy
steps.es: De Bluefields. Es criollo, no inglés.
steps.en: From Bluefields. It is Creole, not English.

options.es: ¿Y allá el español es la segunda lengua?
options.en: And over there Spanish is the second language?
options.feedback: You got straight to the thing that actually surprises people from this side of the country.
Polite and finished. He would have kept going if you had asked anything.

options.en: But that is Nicaragua all the same, is it not?
options.feedback: It is, and phrased like that it sounds like you are correcting him about his own coast.

steps.speaker: Delroy
steps.es: La cuarta, a veces. Primero criollo, inglés y miskito.
steps.en: The fourth, sometimes. First Creole, English and Miskito.

options.es: Chocho, y yo pensaba que aquí era un solo idioma.
options.en: Chocho, and I thought there was one language here.
options.feedback: Admitting what you assumed, out loud, is the fastest way to be told the rest.

options.en: I did not know any of that.
options.feedback: True and fine. It stops just short of asking him for more.

options.es: Yo pensé que todos hablaban español.
options.feedback: Almost the same sentence, said as a fact about the country rather than about you.

steps.speaker: Delroy
steps.es: Casi nadie de aquí ha ido para allá.
steps.en: Almost nobody from here has been over there.

options.es: Yo tampoco. Pero algún día quiero ir.
options.en: Nor have I. But some day I want to go.
options.feedback: You put yourself in the same sentence as everybody else and left a door open. Honest, and he will hold you to it.
Warm and empty. He was telling you something about the country, not about scenery.

options.en: The thing is it is very far.
options.feedback: That is the excuse everybody here gives him. You have just become one more.
